response: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in children with malignancy is a serious condition. Research suggests that it is possible to predict the outcome of ARDS in these children by monitoring certain parameters. Specifically, peak inspiratory pressure, PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure), and ventilation index values can distinguish between survivors and non-survivors by day 3 of treatment. By identifying these predictors early on, healthcare providers may be able to apply supportive nonconventional therapies in a timely manner, potentially improving outcomes for children with malignancy and ARDS.
